newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Violent protests erupt on outskirts of Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Violent protests erupt on outskirts of Bogota.

text.p: Police and army reinforcements were dispatched to a small town on the outskirts of Bogota on Wednesday to quell violent protests against public service price hikes, authorities said.

Red Cross spokesmen said at least one person was killed and more than 20 injured in clashes with security forces that erupted on Tuesday night in Facatativa, a working-class community 18 miles (30 km) west of the capital. The protester died of a gunshot wound to the head, the spokesmen said.

The clashes, in which protesters armed with firebombs and rocks fought pitched battles with riot police, broke out after police moved in to clear barricades that have halted traffic since Monday on a key highway linking the capital to the northwest industrial hub of Medellin and the Atlantic coast.

The protesters went on an all-night rampage in Facatativa after police cleared the barricades, setting fire to the mayor's office and looting or ransacking stores and banks throughout the centre of the town of about 20,000 people.

Alluding to the possible role of leftist guerrillas in the disturbances, which continued on Wednesday when makeshift barricades were again erected across the Medellin highway, Defence Minister Juan Carlos Esguerra said the townspeople of Facatativa were being used by "terrorists."
"They're being used by people interested in disorder, in chaos and in creating anxiety," Esguerra told reporters.
Guerrillas are known to operate out of rural areas near Facatativa but a police spokeswoman said there was no evidence of their direct involvement in the protests.

Protesters interviewed by Reuter Television in Facatativa on Wednesday said their main demand was for a cut in electricity rates, which recently increased in the area by as much as 300 percent. Water prices have undergone similar increases as the government moves to slash public service subsidies, the demontrators said.

"This is about the injustice of the government," said one protester, who identified himself only as a university student. He said police themselves had been responsible for much of the damage in the centre of Facatativa, saying they had used their trucheons to smash windows throughout the area and had also fired tear gas into people's homes.
